newsitem.title: UK: Salvesen braced for stormy EGM, seen winning.
newsitem.headline: Salvesen braced for stormy EGM, seen winning.

text.p: The board of Christian Salvesen Plc faces a stormy extraordinary meeting on Thursday as some investors try to turn the vote on a proposed 100 million stg special dividend into a vote of no-confidence.
Salvesen expects to win backing for the one-off payout but not without having to fight a rearguard action from Sir Gerald Elliot, former chairman of the business services group.

Elliot, a member of the Salvesen family who claims he has 14 percent of shareholder support, plans to lead a shareholder revolt against the dividend and call a vote of no-confidence in the management and for a boardroom purge.
On the one side, Salvesen management want the dividend dealt with separately from its plans for the demerger of its Aggreko division, which will be dealt with at another EGM this year.
But the Elliot camp wants the demerger issue raised on Thursday and will call for a no-confidence vote.
The board is led by chairman Sir Alick Rankin and chief executive Chris Masters.
The protaganist, Elliot said "Many people will want their say at the meeting and a lot of them are unhappy about these proposals." He said the fight would go on even if he lost on Thursday.
One analyst agreed that even if Salvesen won this particular battle, the war would rumble on.
"Problems are not going to go away and although the management should get their way at the EGM it is likely the institutional investors will force changes at the top."
Salvesen has been under attack from investors since rejecting a tentative takeover bid from Hays Plc last year. That would have valued the Scottish-based group at 405 pence per share.

But Salvesen rebuffed the approach, promising to return value to shareholders instead. A special dividend of 17p was paid at the same time as the interim. Its shares currently stand at around 302-1/2p.
